# Theme token reference

The complete vocabulary. A theme assigns literal colors (`#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`) to the required and derived-by-default ids and nothing else. The host draws every `bevel-edge` itself; a theme sets only their strength — see [Bevel](#bevel). It fits every `change-fill` too; a theme sets only the diff hues — see [Change fills](#change-fills).

Authoring guide: [`extend.md`](extend.md#themes).

## Bundled themes

10 themes ship with the app. The two stock units are the cold-start planes — the app paints one of them before any saved choice is restored, so neither can be uninstalled. The rest arrive as the bundled **Themes** extension pack and sit in the picker beside anything a user installs.

| Theme | Id | Appearance | Source |
|-------|----|------------|--------|
| Charcoal | `painted-wolf/platform:charcoal` | dark | Stock — cold-start dark |
| Daylight | `painted-wolf/platform:daylight` | light | Stock — cold-start light |
| Catppuccin Frappé | `painted-wolf/themes:catppuccin-frappe` | dark | Themes pack |
| Catppuccin Latte | `painted-wolf/themes:catppuccin-latte` | light | Themes pack |
| Catppuccin Macchiato | `painted-wolf/themes:catppuccin-macchiato` | dark | Themes pack |
| Catppuccin Mocha | `painted-wolf/themes:catppuccin-mocha` | dark | Themes pack |

## Window colors

`window_colors` declares an open-ended OKLCH color family for active file tabs, peer cursors, selections, and labels. The main window uses `main`; additional native windows use their stable host window number. Removing a window never renumbers or recolors the survivors.

| Field | Default | Bounds and meaning |
|-------|---------|--------------------|
| `main` | `accent-signal` | Opaque hex color for the main window |
| `anchors` | `accent`, `status-positive`, `cost-workers` | 1–12 opaque hex colors defining the peer color family |
| `hue_spread` | 24 | Maximum excursion around each anchor, 0–180 degrees |
| `chroma_min` | 0.04 | Lower OKLCH saturation bound, 0–0.4 |
| `chroma_max` | 0.16 | Upper OKLCH saturation bound, 0–0.4; must be at least `chroma_min` |

The client spreads early slots apart by perceptual distance, then continues sampling the recipe deterministically. Colors are mapped into sRGB by reducing chroma; contrast adjustment may further reduce saturation. Carets clear 3:1 against the editor background (4.5:1 with Increase Contrast); labels clear 4.5:1 (7:1 with Increase Contrast). Selection washes preserve body-text contrast up to the same text floor. An authored main color also passes through those display corrections.

The recipe generates more colors as needed; stable text labels remain the identifier, including for monochrome recipes and forced colors. Runtime theme and OS contrast changes repaint existing identities without replacing the editor or changing its selection. See the [theme authoring guide](extend.md#themes) for an example.

## Agent colors

`agent_colors` declares the colors of agent chats in files: what they read and what they are about to change. Every chat shares one muted hue; each chat is a lightness step away from `main`. A chat keeps its step while it has presence.

| Field | Default | Bounds and meaning |
|-------|---------|--------------------|
| `main` | `text-muted` | Opaque hex color at the center of the family |
| `lightness_step` | 0.1 | OKLCH lightness between neighboring chats, 0.02–0.25 |
| `chroma` | 0.03 | OKLCH saturation of every agent color, 0–0.12 |

Chats alternate lighter and darker around `main`. Carets clear 3:1 against the editor background (4.5:1 with Increase Contrast), and selection washes keep body text legible, so contrast adjustment may move a step. Chat titles on labels remain the identifier.

## Base tokens

Required tokens are the decisions no derivation can make for you. Everything else has a host derivation, so a token added later never invalidates an existing theme.

| Token | Fill | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `background` | required | Page backdrop behind every surface. Must be opaque. |
| `text` | required | Body ink on background and surface. |
| `accent` | required | Accent fill behind on-accent labels (primary buttons). |
| `danger` | required | Destructive and error states. |
| `warning` | required | Caution states, distinct from danger. |
| `status-positive` | required | Success and completion states. |
| `surface` | derived-by-default | Panel and card fill. |
| `surface-elevated` | derived-by-default | Raised surface (menus, popovers). |
| `surface-chrome` | derived-by-default | The plane window chrome sits on: the nav rail, its title bar, and the resize seam that carries the divider. Recessed or lifted relative to the page is the theme's choice — what matters is that chrome reads as frame rather than content. Flat with the page when unset. Setting it moves every mark on the rail with it, not just the fill: see [Planes](#planes). Must be opaque. |
| `surface-inset` | derived-by-default | The track a control is recessed into: a segmented picker or an editor tab strip. The opposite direction from `surface-elevated`. The chosen segment paints `selection` on this track; unchosen labels sit on the track itself. Not a plane: a track's contents keep their own color rather than blending into it, so nothing here follows `--den-plane`. Flat with the page when unset. |
| `brand-field` | derived-by-default | The plate behind the product lockup bars. The product black when unset. A palette that wants the bars on the chrome sets this to that plane, or transparent. Gated against `accent-signal` so the bars cannot vanish into it. |
| `text-muted` | derived-by-default | Secondary ink: captions, metadata, placeholders. |
| `danger-text` | derived-by-default | Destructive and error copy on a surface, as opposed to the fill. Derived from `danger`, darkened or lightened only as far as the legibility floor requires. |
| `warning-text` | derived-by-default | Caution copy on a surface, as opposed to the fill. |
| `status-positive-text` | derived-by-default | Success copy on a surface, as opposed to the fill. |
| `border` | derived-by-default | Hairline rules and control outlines. |
| `shadow` | derived-by-default | The ink elevation shadows are cast in. Body ink on light; true black on dark. |
| `tint-hue` | derived-by-default | Neutral hover hue; the tint ramp derives from it. |
| `surface-offset` | derived-by-default | Wash a seated block sits on — the project cluster, a segmented track. One step off the page: down on light, up on dark. Must be opaque. |
| `surface-raised` | derived-by-default | Plane of something lifted out of a well — the chosen segment in a track. Must read above surface-offset, not below it. Must be opaque. |
| `bevel-highlight` | bevel-edge | Lit edge of a seated block: the top of a raised seam and the bottom of a well. |
| `bevel-shadow` | bevel-edge | Shaded edge of a seated block or a filled plate: under a raised seam and the top of a well. |
| `bevel-plate-highlight` | bevel-edge | Lit edge of a filled plate — a send button, a checked box, a merge action. Lighter than the fill beneath it on every palette, including a pale accent that takes dark label ink. |
| `on-accent` | derived-by-default | Label ink on an accent fill. |
| `accent-warm` | derived-by-default | Secondary accent fill for call-to-action surfaces. |
| `on-accent-warm` | derived-by-default | Label ink on a warm accent fill. Its own decision rather than `on-accent`'s: a palette is free to put the two accents on opposite sides of the luminance line, and then no single ink is readable on both. |
| `accent-text` | derived-by-default | Accent-colored copy on a surface, not a fill. |
| `accent-signal` | derived-by-default | Accent indicators, icons, and links. Also the product lockup bars, which must stay visible on `brand-field`. |
| `accent-hover` | derived-by-default | The accent fill under the pointer. Deepens toward `shadow` when unset, in both schemes: `on-accent` is a light ink, so a hover that lifts the fill takes the label with it. Gated against `on-accent`. |
| `accent-warm-hover` | derived-by-default | `accent-warm` under the pointer, on the same terms as `accent-hover`. |
| `selection` | derived-by-default | Fill behind a selected row, rail item, or segment. Opaque: it sits on the page or a track, so a theme names the color it wants rather than a strength of the accent. |
| `selection-strong` | derived-by-default | Fill behind a selected text range. Heavier than a row selection, which reads from its whole band; a text range has to show its extent character by character. |
| `caret` | derived-by-default | Text insertion caret in the editor and inputs. Body ink when unset, which is what a browser does on its own; a theme that wants the caret to read as its own mark sets it. |
| `status-running` | derived-by-default | In-flight work; distinct from both accent and success. |
| `draft-accent` | derived-by-default | Coordinator draft and orchestration rail. |
| `draft-accent-text` | derived-by-default | Draft-rail copy, quieter than the rail itself. |
| `diff-add-hue` | derived-by-default | Hue for added lines. Separate from status-positive so a theme can make diffs colorblind-safe without changing success. |
| `diff-delete-hue` | derived-by-default | Hue for removed lines. Separate from danger, same reason. |
| `diff-add-line` | change-fill | Fill behind an added line. |
| `diff-add-word` | change-fill | Fill behind the changed words of an added line, painted over `diff-add-line`. |
| `diff-delete-line` | change-fill | Fill behind a removed line. |
| `diff-delete-word` | change-fill | Fill behind the changed words of a removed line, painted over `diff-delete-line`. |
| `cost-coordinator` | derived-by-default | Cost series: coordinator share. |
| `cost-workers` | derived-by-default | Cost series: worker share. |
| `cost-summarizer` | derived-by-default | Cost series: summarizer share. |
| `identity-1` | derived-by-default | Project identity hue 1. The identity set exists to make projects distinguishable at a glance, so the hues stay far apart. |
| `identity-2` | derived-by-default | Project identity hue 2. |
| `identity-3` | derived-by-default | Project identity hue 3. |
| `identity-4` | derived-by-default | Project identity hue 4. |
| `identity-5` | derived-by-default | Project identity hue 5. |

## Planes

`background` and `surface-chrome` are the two *planes* — the opaque surfaces everything else is painted on.

Some marks carry no color of their own and take the plane instead, so they disappear into it: the wash that fades rows out under the Settings dock, the ring cutting the selection dot out of its pill, the ring separating stacked folder tiles, a focus halo. The host tracks which plane each region paints and resolves those marks against it. Set the two planes and the marks follow.

## Bevel

Raised and recessed controls show a lit edge and a shaded edge, drawn in the `bevel-edge` inks above. A theme decides only how strongly they show: `bevel.strength` multiplies every edge's alpha — `1` keeps the product's edges, `0` flattens every control, and `2` doubles them. An edge already at full strength stays there.

```yaml
bevel:
  strength: 0.7
```

A filled plate — a send button, a checked box — takes a white lit edge rather than its label ink, so a pale accent carrying dark text still catches light along its top.

## Change fills

A diff paints two layers in each hue: a fill behind every changed line, and a deeper fill behind the words that changed within it. Code has to stay readable on both, in every syntax color the theme sets, so the host fits the fills to the palette instead of taking them from the theme.

Each ink keeps at least 4.5:1 on a changed word over its line. An ink the theme already sets under that on the page keeps 70% of its page contrast instead. The host lays down as much of each hue as that allows, up to a cap, and gives the line a fixed share of it so a changed word always reads above its line:

| Appearance | Cap | Line share |
|------------|-----|------------|
| light | 30% | 40% |
| dark | 36% | 30% |

A palette with dim syntax colors gets quieter fills rather than unreadable code. To make diffs louder, raise the contrast of the dimmest syntax colors; to recolor them, set `diff-add-hue` and `diff-delete-hue`.

## Icon slots

`icons.stroke` — `weight`, `cap`, `join` — restyles every stroked slot at once, including slots with no geometry below. Weight is a finite 0.5–2.0 multiplier on each slot's host-defined width; stroke never contributes to layout.

`icons.geometry` replaces one slot with the *children* of an `<svg>` on the `0 0 16 16` grid, drawn in `currentColor` or `none`. Shapes are `path`, `circle`, `rect`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, and `g`; path commands, numeric attributes, point lists, and required dimensions are parsed against their SVG grammars, and every shape must draw. Anything that loads, scripts, styles, or references a resource outside the glyph fails to compile. This plane stays partial — a glyph has no derivation, so an unset slot keeps the host's.

The frame is the host's either way: grid, rendered size, paint mode, and each slot's base weight.

## Legibility floor

Security-critical chrome must not be paintable into invisibility. These pairs are measured at compile time; a theme under any minimum fails to compile with a typed diagnostic.

| Foreground | Background | Minimum | Why |
|------------|------------|---------|-----|
| `text` | `background` | 4.5:1 | body text must stay readable |
| `text` | `surface` | 4.5:1 | body text on panels must stay readable |
| `text-muted` | `background` | 3.0:1 | secondary text must stay readable |
| `text` | `surface-chrome` | 4.5:1 | rail and title-bar labels must stay readable |
| `text-muted` | `surface-chrome` | 3.0:1 | rail section headings must stay readable |
| `text-muted` | `surface-inset` | 3.0:1 | an unchosen segment's label must stay readable |
| `danger` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | destructive states must stay visible |
| `danger-text` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | destructive states must stay readable |
| `warning-text` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | caution states must stay readable |
| `status-positive-text` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | success states must stay readable |
| `text` | `selection` | 3.0:1 | a selected row or segment label must stay readable |
| `text` | `selection-strong` | 3.0:1 | selected text must stay readable |
| `on-accent` | `accent` | 4.5:1 | labels on accent fills must stay readable |
| `on-accent` | `accent-hover` | 4.5:1 | labels must stay readable while the pointer is on them |
| `on-accent-warm` | `accent-warm` | 4.5:1 | labels on warm accent fills must stay readable |
| `on-accent-warm` | `accent-warm-hover` | 4.5:1 | labels must stay readable while the pointer is on them |
| `accent-signal` | `brand-field` | 3.0:1 | the product lockup bars must stay visible on their plate |
| `diff-add-hue` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | added lines must be distinguishable from the page |
| `diff-delete-hue` | `surface` | 3.0:1 | removed lines must be distinguishable from the page |
